Title: Withdraws, ousters, and card in play

Messages.Author: Hardrock Llewynyth
Messages.Body:
Just wondering how you people handle the situation of cards in play when
the owner (*not* controller) is ousted or withdraws.

I tend to favor the Sabbat rule that the cards stay in play because it
makes more sense. If i'm playing my FoS and steal vampires, the are now
mine for purposes of the game. As a methusalah, i have wrested control
from another meth and he is dead. The are technically mine.

If i have invested time and blood (Grand Temple of Set) those things
better not disappear when my prey does.

I'm not saying that ownership of the card changes; but control should
still be mine as long as i'm in the game, or someone else steals the
minion or other card (eg, the Rack).

What is you guys' take on this? LSJ?

Hardrock

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
hard...@speakeasy.org (Hardrock Llewynyth) writes:
>Just wondering how you people handle the situation of cards in play when
>the owner (*not* controller) is ousted or withdraws.

>I tend to favor the Sabbat rule that the cards stay in play because it
>makes more sense. If i'm playing my FoS and steal vampires, the are now
>mine for purposes of the game. As a methusalah, i have wrested control
>from another meth and he is dead. The are technically mine.

Not by the Golden Rule of Card Ownership. They are technically burned
when the owner is ousted.

We have alwyas played a house rule that overrules the Golden Rule.
But we recognize that it is just a house rule (partially validated by
the Sabbat rules on withdrawal - note that the Sabbat rules only
apply during withdrawal, not during the standard ousting).

Messages.Author: Hardrock Llewynyth
Messages.Body:
My contention is that The Golden Rule of Card Ownership makes very little
sense *for the purpose of game play* in light of something like FoS or
stolen locations (Disputed Territory, etc). Once the location or minion
has been stolen, it is no longer controlled by the methuselah, so why
should it go away when he does?

Obviously, this does not apply in the case of real life card ownership :)

Hardrock
